summary: This bill expands the types of medical professionals, specifically nurse practitioners, physician assistants, clinical nurse specialists, and certified nurse-midwives, who can provide and be reimbursed for various services under Medicare and Medicaid, including cardiac and pulmonary rehabilitation, diabetes shoe documentation, home infusion therapy, hospice care, and services in skilled nursing facilities, while also clarifying reimbursement for certified registered nurse anesthetists and revising the Medicare local coverage determination process.

scores.thoughts: This bill primarily focuses on expanding the scope of practice and reimbursement for various advanced practice registered nurses (APRNs) within Medicare and Medicaid programs. By allowing nurse practitioners, certified registered nurse anesthetists, and certified nurse-midwives to perform more services and be reimbursed directly, it aims to increase access to healthcare services, particularly for beneficiaries of public programs. This expansion of services by non-physician providers within public health programs leans towards more public healthcare access.

The bill expands the types of services covered and the providers who can deliver them under Medicare and Medicaid, which are key components of the social safety net. By increasing access to care for beneficiaries of these programs, it effectively expands the reach and utility of these welfare programs.
